# Does it run?

Which option trains on real frames under which method? Every option was composed under each method it fits; those accepted were probed on real frames. The few without a record of their own (two adapters compose inserts, two point-painting wrappers, `post=target-mask` and `loss=distribution-focal`, measured inside `decoupled-grid-bins`), the refusals and the options that need your consent are named per option.

## How it was judged {#how-it-was-judged}

- **One cell, one option under one method**: `grasppanda compose <method config> --set <slot>=<option>`, then `grasppanda probe` on the composed config. Measured on: 20 training iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, one run per cell; nothing was measured on GraspClutter6D or on Kinect frames.
- **Four levels, each needing the one before**: `composes` (config accepted), `runs` (trains on real frames without an error), `learns` (its losses fall), `predicts` (it ranks grasps). [Exact definitions](../evidence/index.md#levels).
- **A refusal is the config check's answer**: nothing was built, and the kind says why ([refusal words](../evidence/index.md#refusals)).
- **Undecided counts against**: a method where a level could not be decided stays in the count, named with the reason.
- **One run per cell**: the config hash and the first losses repeat exactly; later numbers may differ in the next run.

??? note "What was run, and how it was judged in detail"

    **1262 recorded cells** (1014 `runs`, 174 `runs-empty`, 29 `runs-unstable`, 41 `refused`, 4 `fails`): every shipped method config as it is, every registered scene encoder under every seed-based method, every variant of every other stage with one stage replaced at a time, every image-encoder preset under HGGD, every post-processing preset under every method (but `target-mask`: reads observation.masks, which no shipped dataset fills), every recipe preset under every method it applies to, every loss preset in one term of each kind it accepts (but `distribution-focal`: fits `bins` terms only, which no shipped method has; probed as the width loss of the head preset `decoupled-grid-bins` (stage cells)), a sample of the sets of stages and a few requests that replace several slots at once. A component that needs an option only a preset supplies (`DepthEmbedGroup`, `DepthPoolGroup`, `MultiRadiusGroup`, `MultiScaleGroup`) has no cell under its type name: that request is refused for the missing option before any contract is compared, which says nothing about a combination. Its presets have cells.

    | Group | Cells recorded | `runs` | `runs-empty` | `runs-unstable` | `refused` | `fails` |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | `reference`: the methods as shipped | 5 of 5 | 4 | 1 | — | — | — |
    | `encoder`: one scene encoder replaced | 235 of 235 | 127 | 90 | 18 | — | — |
    | `stage`: one other stage replaced | 435 of 435 | 382 | 25 | — | 28 | — |
    | `stage-set`: sets of stages | 95 of 9104 | 86 | 9 | — | — | — |
    | `family`: other detector families, as shipped | 1 of 1 | 1 | — | — | — | — |
    | `family-slot`: one component of another detector family replaced | 38 of 38 | 35 | 2 | — | 1 | — |
    | `post`: one post-processing step as the variant `post` | 84 of 84 | 70 | 14 | — | — | — |
    | `loss`: one loss of one stage replaced | 134 of 134 | 119 | 11 | — | 4 | — |
    | `recipe`: one recipe preset applied (optimizer, schedule, hooks, augmentation) | 217 of 217 | 179 | 15 | 11 | 8 | 4 |
    | `cross`: options of several slots replaced together | 18 of 18 | 11 | 7 | — | — | — |
    | **all** | **1262 of 10271** | **1014** | **174** | **29** | **41** | **4** |

    - **A cell**: `grasppanda compose <method config> --set <slot>=<choice>` (so an encoder is fitted and adapters are inserted exactly as a user gets them), then `grasppanda probe <composed config> --iters 20 --frames 8 --schedule constant`: the real trainer with the method's own recipe on the split `sample` of GraspNet-1Billion (RealSense; scene 0, frames 0, 32, …, 224), then prediction on two of those frames. Both commands of every cell are in the [records](measured_combinations.json).
    - **The learning rate**: the recipe's peak rate at every step (`--schedule constant`), scaled by the ratio of the batch sizes when the probe's batches are smaller (FineGrasp's 0.008 for 32 frames trains at 0.002 on 8); the optimizer, weight decay, clipping and hooks as the recipe has them. Over the few epochs of a probe the schedules would decay some methods far more than others, and the trends would not compare. A request that sets the schedule (a schedule preset, a schedule-free optimizer, a recipe preset) runs that schedule. Of the 1182 probes on this page, 1103 held the peak rate (`schedule: constant` in the record); 79 ran the recipe's schedule (`schedule: recipe`).
    - **One exception to "as a user gets them"**: configs that read the width histogram of Scale-Balanced-Grasp were probed with the reference's own file (`scale_statistic.source: legacy_import`): the native histogram is a statistic of the whole training split, and a probe reads eight frames.
    - **Two cells with one config are one experiment**: a cell that composes to the config of another cell (the same config hash) shares its probe; 39 of the 1262 cells do. A cell that composes to its method's shipped config is the method's own component and is not counted as a swap.
    - **When and where**: 3 cells on 2026-10-15 with GraspPanda at commit `0ddca31`, PyTorch 2.7.1+cu118, Python 3.12.7, on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs, 2 probes at a time. 288 cells on 2026-10-15 with GraspPanda at commit `2a3760a`, PyTorch 2.7.1+cu118, Python 3.12.7, on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs, 2 probes at a time. 538 cells on 2026-10-15 with GraspPanda at commit `96facee`, PyTorch 2.7.1+cu118, Python 3.12.7, on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs, 2 probes at a time. 430 cells on 2026-10-15 with GraspPanda at commit `98e5310`, PyTorch 2.7.1+cu118, Python 3.12.7, on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs, 2 probes at a time. 3 cells on 2026-10-16 with GraspPanda at commit `96facee`, PyTorch 2.7.1+cu118, Python 3.12.7, on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs, 2 probes at a time.

    **1221 of the 1262 records** on this page were judged by judge 2 (`judge: 2` in the records), which also records whether the parts of a model learned: the trend of every loss term, the units no gradient reached, the parts that did not change and the spread of the scores. A record of the first judge has none of it, so its `learns` and `predicts` are undecided (not checked). The loss of every iteration of every probe of judge 2 is in [measured_combinations/losses_per_iteration.json](measured_combinations/losses_per_iteration.json).

    The flags of a loss term, named in the tails (*active* iterations: the term was reported, finite and not exactly 0):

    - `flat`: the term was active in at least two iterations, and the mean of its last quarter differs from its first active value by less than 5 % of that value.
    - `rising`: the term was active in at least two iterations, and the mean of the last half of its active iterations exceeds the mean of the first half by more than 10 % of the first half's mean (with an odd count the middle iteration is in neither half).
    - `zero_at_end`: the term is exactly 0.0, or not reported, at the last completed iteration.
    - `constant`: the term was reported in at least two iterations with the very same value in every one of them, zeros included.

    The schedules of a probe (`schedule` in a record):

    - `recipe`: the config's own scheduler, run over the probe. The probe sets `train.epochs` to ceil(iterations / iterations per epoch), so a schedule that steps per epoch is compressed into those few epochs (GSNet's 0.95 per epoch ends at 0.95^9 = 0.63 after 20 iterations of 2 per epoch, EconomicGrasp's cosine at 2.4 % of its start) and one that steps per iteration runs its first steps only (FineGrasp's warm-up of 800 iterations keeps a probe of 20 at no more than 2.5 % of its rate).
    - `constant`: no scheduler: every parameter group of every optimizer trains at the recipe's peak rate for the whole probe. The peak is the rate the optimizer gives the group (the configured `lr`, with the multipliers of ParamGroups), except for a schedule that sets a peak of its own: `max_lr` of OneCycleLR and CyclicLR, the larger factor of LinearLR. Every other schedule of the toolbox starts at that rate or reaches it at the end of its warm-up. When the probe's batches hold fewer frames than the recipe's, the peak is scaled by their ratio (the linear scaling rule: FineGrasp's 0.008 for 32 frames trains at 0.002 on batches of 8). A batch-norm momentum that the recipe decays per epoch (BNMomentumHook: GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp, HGGD) is held at its first epoch's value likewise (`hooks.<i>.decay=1`): decayed over epochs of a few iterations it can reach its floor of 0.001 within the probe (Scale-Balanced-Grasp's at iteration 73), and the running statistics, which prediction normalises with, then stop following the weights; training itself does not read them. The optimizer (its weight decay and its momentum as configured), clipping, accumulation and every other hook are the recipe's.

    **Passed the check, failed afterwards.**

    4 cell(s) passed the config check and failed afterwards: each group is a gap between what the config check knows and what the components need (*N* stands for a number that differs from cell to cell).

    - **at step: RuntimeError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.** 1 cell(s): `recipe/HGGD/optimizer/soap`.
    - **at hook, in the hook SWAHook: EngineError: SWAHook.start_epoch is N, but the run has N epochs: nothing would be averaged.** 2 cell(s): `recipe/GraspNet-baseline/hooks/swa`, `recipe/Scale-Balanced-Grasp/hooks/swa`.
    - **at data, in the transform DepthNormals: ContractError: DepthNormals must run before the cloud of graspnet1b<path> is sampled: put it first in `transforms`.** 1 cell(s): `recipe/FineGrasp/augment/dropout`.

    - `hooks=accumulate-2`: *runs*: own in HGGD · *predicts*: FineGrasp undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either) · *trains like shipped*: worse under GraspNet-baseline, GSNet, EconomicGrasp
    - `hooks=agc`: *learns*: not FineGrasp (does not learn: angle rising) · *predicts*: Scale-Balanced-Grasp undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either)
    - `hooks=amp`: *runs*: not GraspNet-baseline, GSNet, Scale-Balanced-Grasp, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, HGGD (not supported yet)
    - `hooks=ema`: *learns*: HGGD undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either) · *predicts*: Scale-Balanced-Grasp, FineGrasp undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either)
    - `hooks=freeze-encoder`: *runs*: not FineGrasp (unstable twice in the short probe) · *learns*: not GSNet (does not learn: objectness flat; graspness rose 8 %); not EconomicGrasp (does not learn: objectness flat; graspness flat) · *trains like shipped*: not compared under FineGrasp: the swap did not run at level 1
    - `hooks=grad-clip`: *predicts*: Scale-Balanced-Grasp, FineGrasp undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either) · *trains like shipped*: worse under FineGrasp
    - `hooks=swa`: *runs*: not GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp (not verified: the probe is shorter than the epoch at which averaging starts) · *predicts*: FineGrasp undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either)
    - `augment=dropout`: *runs*: not FineGrasp (fails: the transform order of the composed config is wrong (DepthNormals must run first)) · *learns*: HGGD undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either) · *predicts*: Scale-Balanced-Grasp undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either)
    - `augment=jitter`: *runs*: not HGGD (not supported yet) · *predicts*: FineGrasp undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either)
    - `augment=shift`: *runs*: not HGGD (not supported yet) · *predicts*: Scale-Balanced-Grasp, FineGrasp undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either) · *trains like shipped*: worse under EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp
    - `recipe=adamw-onecycle`: *predicts*: Scale-Balanced-Grasp undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either) · *trains like shipped*: not compared under GraspNet-baseline, GSNet, Scale-Balanced-Grasp, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, HGGD: it trained on a schedule of its own, not on that of the method as shipped
    - `recipe=finetune-encoder`: *runs*: not FineGrasp (unstable twice in the short probe) · *learns*: not GSNet (does not learn: objectness flat; graspness rose 152 %); not EconomicGrasp (does not learn: objectness flat; graspness rose 165 %) · *predicts*: Scale-Balanced-Grasp undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either) · *trains like shipped*: not compared under GraspNet-baseline, GSNet, Scale-Balanced-Grasp, EconomicGrasp: it trained on a schedule of its own, not on that of the method as shipped; not compared under FineGrasp: the swap did not run at level 1
    - `recipe=ptv3-adamw-onecycle`: *predicts*: Scale-Balanced-Grasp undecided (the method as shipped does not reach it in a short run either) · *trains like shipped*: not compared under GraspNet-baseline, GSNet, Scale-Balanced-Grasp, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp: it trained on a schedule of its own, not on that of the method as shipped

    </div>

    A preset that names the scene encoder (`optimizer=encoder-lr-0.1`, `optimizer=layer-decay`, `hooks=freeze-encoder`, `recipe=finetune-encoder`, `recipe=ptv3-adamw-onecycle`) applies to the seed-based methods only: HGGD has no scene encoder.

## Sets of stages {#sets-of-stages}

A set replaces the encoder and every stage at once. The rules accept 9104 sets of stage options (per kind of encoder output); **95 were probed** (86 `runs`, 9 `runs-empty`), covering 118 of the 118 pairs of a stage variant and a kind of encoder. A set that runs says nothing about another set with the same parts.

??? note "The probed sets, by the method whose data recipe serves their labels"

    | Data recipe of | Sets probed | `runs` | `runs-empty` |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | GraspNet-baseline | 16 | 16 | — |
    | GSNet | 35 | 30 | 5 |
    | Scale-Balanced-Grasp | 21 | 17 | 4 |
    | EconomicGrasp | 23 | 23 | — |

    Every probed set, with its request and its verdict, is in the [records](measured_combinations.json) (group `stage-set`). [Swap rules](swapping.md#every-legal-set-of-stages) counts the same rules over registered classes: 3014 sets.

## The records {#the-records}

[measured_combinations.json](measured_combinations.json) holds every cell: its two commands, its verdict, why it was refused or failed, and what the probe saw; [losses_per_iteration.json](measured_combinations/losses_per_iteration.json) every loss term at every iteration. The [explorer](../explorer/index.md) answers any selection from them, with the command.

??? note "Add a component to the grid"

    A new encoder or stage enters the grid by being registered. Give it a preset if its options cannot be guessed ([Compose and probe](../user_guides/combinations.md)), probe its cells and regenerate. `tests/unit/test_combine_grid.py` fails until every cell of a registered component has a record.

    ```bash
    python -m tools.probe_grid run --only 'encoder/*/MyEncoder' 'stage/*/*/my-preset'
    python -m tools.probe_grid export
    python -m tools.make_combination_docs
    ```
